title: Having a partner at the birth
what: Someone close to you stays with you during labor. They support you and help you breathe and change position.
why: When you want your husband, mother, or another close person with you. It is your choice.
duration: usually for the whole labor; the exact rules depend on the maternity hospital
tell_doctor: If you want a partner at the birth. Say so ahead of time
If your partner has the tests the hospital requires
Your wishes: what your partner can and cannot do

prepare.title: Hospital rules
prepare.text: Find out ahead of time what tests and documents your partner needs.

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: It helps if your partner goes to childbirth classes.

prepare.title: Partner's clothes
prepare.text: Clean clothes and shoes to change into, sometimes a disposable gown.

bring: Your partner's test results, if required
Clothes and shoes for your partner to change into
Water and a snack for your partner
steps: Your partner comes with you or later, following the hospital rules
During contractions, they help you breathe and massage your lower back
They help you change position and give you water
They follow the instructions of the doctors and midwife
After the birth, they can stay with you and the baby
feel: Support from someone close usually helps you get through contractions more calmly
It can be hard for your partner to see you in pain. This is normal
after: Your partner can help with the baby's first breastfeed
Usually your partner leaves after the observation period in the delivery room. The hospital will tell you the rules
red_flags: If your partner feels unwell, they should tell the staff right away and step out

faq.q: Can my partner leave during the birth?
faq.a: Yes, at any time. The staff will tell you when is best.

faq.q: What should my partner do if the doctors are busy?
faq.a: Stay out of the way, hold your hand, and do what the staff ask.

reminders.text: Reminder: check that your partner's documents and tests for the maternity hospital are ready.
